title: Effects of Creatine Supplementation and Resistance Training on Muscle Strength Gains in Adults <50 Years of Age: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
population: Adults under 50 years; 23 studies (20 in males, 2 in females, 1 mixed)
intervention: Creatine supplementation combined with resistance training vs placebo
outcomes: Greater upper-body (WMD 4.43 kg) and lower-body (WMD 11.35 kg) strength gains vs placebo; gains significant in males, not in females.
summary: Meta-analysis: creatine plus resistance training increased upper- and lower-body strength in adults under 50, with larger benefits likely in males than females.

title: Effects of creatine supplementation on cognitive function of healthy individuals: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
population: Healthy individuals (6 RCTs, 281 participants)
outcomes: Short-term memory and intelligence/reasoning may improve; results for other cognitive domains conflicting; no change in young individuals; vegetarians responded better than meat-eaters on memory tasks.
limitations: Effects on most cognitive domains unclear; authors call for larger samples.
summary: Systematic review: creatine may improve short-term memory and reasoning in healthy people, with potential benefit suggested for aging and stressed individuals.

title: Meta-analysis: melatonin for the treatment of primary sleep disorders.
population: Adults and children with primary sleep disorders (19 studies, 1683 participants)
outcomes: Sleep latency 7.06 min shorter, total sleep time 8.25 min longer, overall sleep quality improved (SMD 0.22); longer trials and higher doses showed larger effects on latency and total sleep time.
limitations: Effects are modest and smaller than those of other prescription sleep medicines.
summary: Meta-analysis: melatonin modestly shortened sleep-onset latency and lengthened total sleep time, and the effects did not fade with continued use.

title: Oral magnesium supplementation for insomnia in older adults: a Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis.
population: Older adults with insomnia (3 RCTs, 151 participants)
dose: Less than 1 g, up to three times a day (authors' conclusion)
outcomes: Sleep onset latency 17.36 min shorter vs placebo; total sleep time 16.06 min longer, not statistically significant.
limitations: All trials at moderate-to-high risk of bias; low to very low quality of evidence.
summary: Systematic review: the evidence is too weak for firm recommendations, though RCT evidence may support oral magnesium for insomnia symptoms in older adults.

title: Comparison of vitamin D2 and vitamin D3 supplementation in raising serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D status: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
population: Adults in RCTs directly comparing vitamin D2 and D3
outcomes: D3 raised serum 25(OH)D more than D2 (P = 0.001); the advantage held for bolus doses but was lost with daily supplementation.
limitations: Effects across age, sex and ethnicity could not be verified.
summary: Meta-analysis: vitamin D3 raised serum 25(OH)D more effectively than D2, particularly when given as a bolus.

title: Association Between Omega-3 Fatty Acid Intake and Dyslipidemia: A Continuous Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
population: 90 RCTs, 72,598 participants
intervention: Omega-3 fatty acids (DHA, EPA or both)
dose: Dose-response modelled; near-linear effects most evident at medium to high doses (>2 g/d)
outcomes: Near-linear, dose-dependent lowering of triglycerides and non-HDL cholesterol; J-shaped curves for LDL and HDL cholesterol.
summary: Dose-response meta-analysis: omega-3 intake lowered triglycerides and non-HDL cholesterol roughly in proportion to dose.

title: Efficacy of omega-3 PUFAs in depression: A meta-analysis.
population: 26 double-blind, placebo-controlled RCTs (2160 participants)
dose: EPA ≤1 g/d in the formulations showing benefit
outcomes: Overall benefit on depression symptoms (SMD -0.28); EPA-pure and EPA-major (≥60% EPA) formulations showed benefit, DHA-pure and DHA-major did not.
summary: Meta-analysis: omega-3 formulations with at least 60% EPA, at up to 1 g/d EPA, were associated with improved depression symptoms.

title: Effects of Tea (Camellia sinensis) or its Bioactive Compounds l-Theanine or l-Theanine plus Caffeine on Cognition, Sleep, and Mood in Healthy Participants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
population: Healthy participants (50 RCTs reviewed, 15 meta-analysed)
intervention: Tea, L-theanine alone, or L-theanine plus caffeine vs placebo
duration: Acute; outcomes in the first and second hour after intake
outcomes: Small-to-moderate differences favouring theanine plus caffeine on choice reaction time, digit vigilance accuracy, attention-switching accuracy and mood; theanine alone favoured on choice reaction time.
limitations: Confidence intervals frequently left the direction and size of the effects uncertain.
summary: Meta-analysis: theanine plus caffeine, and theanine alone, could benefit short-term cognition and mood, but wide confidence intervals leave the size and direction of the effects uncertain.

title: L-Theanine reduces psychological and physiological stress responses.
population: 12 participants
intervention: L-theanine vs placebo vs nothing, double-blind, counterbalanced, during a mental arithmetic stress task
outcomes: Smaller heart-rate and salivary IgA responses to acute stress vs placebo; heart-rate variability suggested reduced sympathetic activation.
summary: Small crossover study: L-theanine reduced physiological stress responses to an acute mental task.

title: Glycine ingestion improves subjective sleep quality in human volunteers, correlating with polysomnographic changes
population: Not reported in abstract
outcomes: Not reported in abstract
summary: Not reported in abstract

title: A standardized Ashwagandha root extract alleviates stress, anxiety, and improves quality of life in healthy adults by modulating stress hormones: Results from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
population: Healthy adults with mild to moderate stress and anxiety (54 randomised, 50 completed)
intervention: Ashwagandha root extract standardised to 2.5% withanolides, with piperine, vs placebo
dose: 500 mg extract (12.5 mg withanolides) with 5 mg piperine, once daily at night
outcomes: Perceived stress, anxiety (GAD-7) and quality-of-life scores improved vs placebo; morning salivary cortisol fell more and urinary serotonin rose; NO, GSH and MDA unchanged.
summary: Randomized, double-blind trial: the extract reduced perceived stress and anxiety and lowered morning cortisol vs placebo in healthy adults.

title: The Effect of Berberine on Metabolic Profiles in Type 2 Diabetic Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (46 RCTs)
intervention: Berberine alone or with standard diabetes therapy vs control
outcomes: Lower HbA1c (MD -0.73), fasting glucose (MD -0.86) and 2-h postprandial glucose (MD -1.26); improved insulin-resistance measures; lower triglycerides and higher HDL.
summary: Meta-analysis: berberine, alone or added to standard therapy, improved glycaemic and lipid measures in type 2 diabetes.

title: Zinc for prevention and treatment of the common cold.
population: Children and adults (34 RCTs, 8526 participants)
intervention: Zinc in any form (mostly lozenges: acetate, gluconate or orotate) vs placebo, for prevention or during a cold
dose: Zinc gluconate lozenges 45-276 mg/day; other forms not reported in abstract
duration: Gluconate lozenges 4.5-21 days; prevention follow-up 5-18 months
outcomes: Little or no effect on catching a cold; when taken during a cold, duration may be shorter (MD -2.37 days, low certainty); non-serious adverse events probably more frequent.
limitations: Most studies at unclear or high risk of bias; wide variation in interventions and outcomes; incomplete reporting.
summary: Cochrane review: zinc may shorten ongoing colds (low-certainty evidence) but probably does not prevent them, and non-serious side effects are more common.

title: Zinc supplementation and status markers
population: Populations at risk of zinc deficiency
outcomes: Supplementation restored zinc status in deficient groups.
summary: Confirms zinc supplementation corrects deficiency in at-risk populations.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional vitamin B12 status among adult vegans.
population: Adult vegans compared with vegetarians and omnivores (19 studies; 17 meta-analysed)
intervention: Observational diet comparison; subgroup of vitamin B12 supplement users among vegans
outcomes: Vegans had lower serum B12 and higher homocysteine than omnivores; vegans using B12 supplements had better values on all B12 biomarkers than non-users.
limitations: Serum B12 alone has limited sensitivity and specificity for functional deficiency.
summary: Meta-analysis: vegan adults showed lower B12 status, and B12 supplement use among vegans was associated with better status on every measured biomarker.

title: Caffeine and cognitive performance: a review
population: Healthy adults
outcomes: Consistent improvements in alertness, vigilance, and reaction time.
limitations: Tolerance and withdrawal can confound habitual users.
summary: Robust acute cognitive benefits; effects partly offset by tolerance.

title: Effects of Caffeine Intake on Endurance Running Performance and Time to Exhaustion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
population: 254 recreational and trained runners, mostly men (21 crossover RCTs)
outcomes: Time to exhaustion improved (g = 0.392, medium); running time-trial times shorter (g = -0.101, small).
limitations: Few women studied; best dose not established.
summary: Meta-analysis: acute caffeine improved endurance running performance in recreational and trained runners.

title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults.
population: Healthy adults in resistance-training RCTs (49 studies, 1863 participants)
intervention: Dietary protein supplementation with resistance training
dose: No further fat-free-mass gain beyond ~1.6 g/kg/day total protein
duration: Resistance training of at least 6 weeks
outcomes: Greater gains in 1-RM strength (2.49 kg), fat-free mass (0.30 kg) and muscle size; effect smaller with age and larger in resistance-trained people.
summary: Meta-analysis: protein supplementation enhanced resistance-training gains in strength and muscle size, up to about 1.6 g/kg/day total protein.

title: The Effects of an Oral Taurine Dose and Supplementation Period on Endurance Exercise Performance in Humans: A Meta-Analysis.
population: Participants in 10 studies (7 time-to-exhaustion trials)
dose: 1-6 g/day; dose did not change the effect
outcomes: Endurance performance improved (g = 0.40), similarly in time-to-exhaustion trials (g = 0.43); acute and chronic supplementation did not differ.
summary: Meta-analysis: a single oral dose of taurine (1-6 g) improved endurance performance.

title: N-acetylcysteine and glutathione status
population: Adults
outcomes: Increased glutathione availability.
limitations: Biomarker endpoint; clinical translation varies by context.
summary: Reliably supports glutathione synthesis; downstream benefits are context-specific.

title: Oral Magnesium Supplementation for Treating Glucose Metabolism Parameters in People with or at Risk of Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trials.
population: People with diabetes or at high risk of diabetes
outcomes: Lower fasting glucose in diabetes; in people at high risk, better plasma glucose, 2-h oral glucose tolerance results and insulin-sensitivity markers.
summary: Meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs: oral magnesium improved glucose measures in diabetes and may improve insulin sensitivity in people at high risk.

title: Creatine supplementation effect on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
population: Participants in 9 trials of exercise-induced muscle damage
outcomes: Lower creatine kinase overall (WMD -30.94) and at 48, 72 and 96 h; lactate dehydrogenase not significantly lower overall.
limitations: High heterogeneity and medium risk of bias; authors advise caution.
summary: Meta-analysis: creatine lowered creatine kinase after muscle-damaging exercise, though heterogeneity was high.

title: Omega-3 fatty acids for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease.
population: Adults at varying cardiovascular risk (86 RCTs, 162,796 participants)
intervention: More long-chain omega-3 (mostly capsules) or ALA vs usual or lower intake
dose: Long-chain omega-3 from 0.5 g to more than 5 g a day
outcomes: Little or no effect of long-chain omega-3 on all-cause mortality (RR 0.97) or cardiovascular events; may slightly reduce coronary heart disease deaths and events; triglycerides about 15% lower.
limitations: Only 28 of 86 trials at low summary risk of bias.
summary: Cochrane review: more long-chain omega-3 had little or no effect on all-cause mortality, may slightly reduce coronary heart disease events, and lowered triglycerides.

title: The influence of creatine supplementation on the cognitive functioning of vegetarians and omnivores.
population: 128 young adult women, vegetarian or omnivore
outcomes: No effect on verbal fluency or vigilance; better memory in vegetarians but not in meat-eaters; less variable choice reaction times in both groups.
summary: RCT: five days of creatine improved memory in vegetarian but not in omnivorous young women.

title: Impact of omega-3 fatty acids on hypertriglyceridemia, lipidomics, and gut microbiome in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: 309 Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia
intervention: Fish oil vs corn oil, double-blind
outcomes: Larger triglyceride reduction with fish oil (-1.51 vs -0.66 mmol/L); minor effects on gut microbiota; baseline microbiota predicted the triglyceride response.
summary: RCT: fish oil lowered triglycerides more than corn oil in type 2 diabetes with hypertriglyceridemia.

title: Does Ashwagandha supplementation have a beneficial effect on the management of anxiety and stress? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
population: 12 RCTs, 1,002 participants aged 25-48
dose: Favourable effect on stress at 300-600 mg/d (dose-response analysis)
outcomes: Lower anxiety (SMD -1.55) and stress (SMD -1.75) vs placebo.
limitations: Low certainty of evidence for both outcomes; I² 83-94%.
summary: Meta-analysis: ashwagandha reduced stress and anxiety vs placebo, with low certainty of evidence.

title: Faster but not smarter: effects of caffeine and caffeine withdrawal on alertness and performance.
population: 369 adults: 212 medium-high and 157 non-low habitual caffeine consumers
intervention: Caffeine vs placebo after overnight abstinence, double-blind
outcomes: Caffeine reversed withdrawal effects in medium-high consumers; in non-low consumers it reduced sleepiness but raised anxiety/jitteriness, with little net gain in alertness or mental performance; motor performance improved in both groups.
summary: RCT: because of tolerance, habitual caffeine use gave little net gain in mental alertness beyond reversing withdrawal, though motor performance improved.
